title: AVL left rotation with a grandchild
summary: A left rotation promotes the unbalanced node’s right child. That child’s former left child attaches to the right of the demoted node, restoring balance and preserving binary search tree order.
context: There are 6 nodes before rotation. Root 1 has left child 0 and right child 4; 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 5 has only a right child, 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. The variable node points to unbalanced root 1, child to its right child 4, and grand_child to 4’s left child 3.

The balance factor is left subtree height minus right subtree height. A leaf has height 0 and an empty subtree has height −1. The tree is balanced when every node’s factor has absolute value at most 1. The values below follow from the links in the figure.
Before rotation root 1 has left subtree height 0 and right subtree height 2, so its balance factor is −2. It needs a left rotation.
description: Three panels from left to right show the original tree, the completed left rotation with the grandchild reattached, and the tidied layout with old dashed positions removed.

The left rotation promotes child (4) to root and makes node (1) its left child. Node 1 thus occupies the place that belonged to grandchild 3 under 4. Since 1 < 3 < 4, attaching 3 to the right of 1 preserves the strict ordering of the binary search tree.
result: After rotation, both subtrees of the new root 4 have height 1. The entire tree is balanced, and all 6 nodes retain their inorder sequence [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6].

frames.title: AVL left rotation with a grandchild
frames.explanation: First save node 3 with grand_child = child.left. Next, child.left = node makes 1 the left child of 4, and node.right = grand_child makes 3 the right child of 1. Node 0 remains left of 1, and 5 with its right child 6 stays right of 4. In the middle panel pale dashed outlines mark the former positions of 1 and 0, with dashed lines from the old 1 to the old 0 and to node 4. These marks track movement; there are no extra nodes. The last panel removes them and adjusts the layout without another rotation.

steps.title: Locate the unbalanced node and the grandchild to reattach
steps.explanation: Before rotation: Root 1 has left child 0 and right child 4; 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 5 has only a right child, 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. Here node=1, child=4, and grand_child=3, for 6 nodes in total. The root’s left and right heights are 0 and 2, giving balance factor −2. Save 4’s left child 3 before the left rotation overwrites its link.
steps.key_state: Root 1 has left child 0 and right child 4; 4 has left child 3 and right child 5; 5 has only a right child, 6. The root’s balance factor is −2. Grandchild 3 awaits reattachment.
steps.announcement: Locate unbalanced root 1, its right child 4, and grandchild 3 to be reattached.

steps.title: Rotate left and reattach grandchild 3
steps.explanation: Left rotation complete. Root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has left child 0 and right child 3; 5 has only a right child, 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. Since 1<3<4, node 3 can move from the left of 4 to the right of 1. Dashed circles at the old positions of 1 and 0, and dashed links from the old 1 to the old 0 and to 4, show the previous layout only. There are still 6 nodes.
steps.key_state: Root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has left child 0 and right child 3; 5 has only a right child, 6. Dashed lines show former positions only.
steps.announcement: 4 becomes root, 1 becomes the left child of 4, and grandchild 3 becomes the right child of 1.

steps.title: Remove the dashed outlines and tidy the layout
steps.explanation: The old dashed positions disappear and the layout is tidied. The links stay the same. Root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has left child 0 and right child 3; 5 has only a right child, 6. Nodes 0, 3, and 6 are leaves. No second rotation occurs. Both subtrees of root 4 have height 1 and the tree is balanced.
steps.key_state: Dashed outlines removed; no second rotation. Root 4 has left child 1 and right child 5; 1 has left child 0 and right child 3; 5 has only a right child, 6. Both sides have height 1.
steps.announcement: Remove the dashed old positions and tidy the layout to show the balanced AVL tree.
